Atmospheric Police: Delegated Authority in the Clean Development Mechanism\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400848669-008\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2013, 12, 31]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2307/j.ctt5hhqdr.10\", \"title\": [\"Atmospheric Police:\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2307/j.ctt5hhqdr.10\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2013, 12, 22]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5220/0014490000004052\", \"title\": [\"Assessing Moral Frameworks for Autonomous Vehicle Decision-Making\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5220/0014490000004052\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6316039\", \"title\": [\"Delegated Brokerage in Fragmented Governance: Interpretive Authority and Regional Mediation in Initiative-Based Order\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This research develops a theory of interpretive delegation and delegated brokerage to explain how authority is redistributed under initiative-based governance in fragmented institutional environments. It argues that when major powers expand influence through broadly articulated initiatives, rather than through treaty replacement, and embed these initiatives within existing multilateral institutions, centralized interpretive control becomes structurally diluted. Because initiative principles are under-specified, partially embedded, and dependent on multi-level translation for implementation, authority over meaning is redistributed downward. This redistribution does not occur through formal contractual delegation but through structural necessity, generating what the research terms interpretive delegation. Building on this structural condition, the research introduces delegated brokerage to capture the active political process through which cohesive regional organizations convert interpretive authority into procedural leverage. Brokerage operates through four mechanisms: language shaping, agenda framing, coalition bridging, and procedural sequencing. Under conditions of high normative ambiguity and sufficient regional cohesion, regional actors can shape institutional outputs disproportionate to their material power. Fragmentation, therefore, does not simply generate disorder; it can produce a mediated form of order in which authority circulates through interpretive practice rather than centralized rule-making. Through structured comparisons across development governance, security governance, and AI governance, the research demonstrates that delegated brokerage is conditional. In highly ambiguous and decentralized domains such as development and emerging technology governance, regional mediation is more likely. In centralized and politically sensitive domains such as security governance, interpretive space narrows, and brokerage is constrained. The research contributes to global governance theory in three ways. First, it reconceptualizes fragmentation as vertical authority redistribution rather than mere horizontal institutional proliferation. Second, it extends delegation theory by identifying a non-contractual, structural form of authority transfer rooted in interpretive practice. Third, it theorizes regional organizations not as passive arenas of great-power competition but as mediating nodes capable of shaping institutional meaning within fragmented systems. As soft-law initiatives and principle-based governance expand, the politics of interpretation will increasingly structure institutional resilience under geopolitical competition.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6316039\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "a5729252da9ff8c7e452f6c60e80a9b1c24729f0a3981b0992abdfe2145e19c1", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "responsibility_formation", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1515/9781400848669-008", "doi:10.2307/j.ctt5hhqdr.10", "doi:10.5220/0014490000004052", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6316039"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400848669-008", "https://doi.org/10.2307/j.ctt5hhqdr.10", "https://doi.org/10.5220/0014490000004052", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6316039"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
